\section{Hostile cases and invariance checks}\label{app:stress}

The theorem was tested against the following failure modes.

\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.27\textwidth}p{0.31\textwidth}p{0.34\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Case & Expected behavior & Result and mathematical consequence\\
\midrule
\endhead
No tree gauge & Gauge zero modes remain & $d_1$ has an $80$-dimensional scalar kernel; coercivity is asserted only after the based quotient.\\
Twenty-four independent face variables & Rank is overstated & Exact elimination returns rank $17$ and fixes the fiber dimension at $119$.\\
Reverse spanning tree & Coordinate matrix changes & A second exact $LDL^{\mathsf T}$ certificate still proves the floor $1/25$.\\
Link orientation flips & Columns change sign & The Gram matrix changes by diagonal sign congruence and the floor is preserved.\\
Radius $r\ge1/2$ & Banach logarithm denominator closes & The verifier raises an error and emits no certificate.\\
Heat time above $10^{-18}$ & Declared image lemma is unavailable & The verifier fails closed rather than extrapolating the bound.\\
Chart boundary & Strict margins must remain positive & Exact fraction comparison gives $\kappa<1/1000$ and $\eta<1/400$ on the closed chart.\\
Hard fiber boundary & Differentiation may acquire a moving boundary term & The domain $\cD_r$ is independent of $y$; convex barriers justify Brascamp--Lieb.\\
Reference tail promoted to interacting tail & Normalization is missing & Explicitly rejected; Proposition~\ref{prop:reference-tail} is labeled Gaussian only.\\
Finite matrix floor promoted to mass & Physical scaling and reconstruction are missing & Explicitly rejected in title, theorem, discussion, and conclusion.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

These cases do not prove that an implementation is correct, but they expose
the assumptions most likely to generate a false strengthening of the theorem.
